response.sql:
WITH filtered_fees AS (
  SELECT 
    orderslink,
    rebtotal,
    CASE WHEN feerate IS NOT NULL THEN rebrate / feerate ELSE NULL END AS ratio
  FROM fees
  WHERE rebrate >= 0.0005
),
per_order_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    orderslink,
    AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal,
    AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio
  FROM filtered_fees
  GROUP BY orderslink
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_ratio
  FROM per_order_stats
)
SELECT 
  pos.orderslink,
  pos.avg_rebtotal,
  pos.avg_ratio,
  CASE 
    WHEN om.mean_ratio IS NOT NULL 
    THEN pos.avg_ratio / om.mean_ratio
    ELSE NULL
  END AS relative_ratio
FROM per_order_stats pos
CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
ORDER BY relative_ratio DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The rebate-to-fee ratio calculation (rebrate / feerate) excludes records with NULL feerate, meaning rebtotal and ratio averages may draw from different record subsets within each order.

alternatives.interpretation: "Ignoring missing values" could mean filtering to records with both non-NULL rebtotal and non-NULL feerate before computing both averages jointly on this filtered set, rather than handling each missing value independently.
